title: Diffusion Model as a Noise-Aware Latent Reward Model for Step-Level Preference Optimization
role: The closest noise-aware text and image score: it reads noisy SDXL latents through U-Net features, but uses the score to pick training pairs and never takes its gradient.
reads: Noisy latent and timestep through the U-Net, down and middle features average pooled over space, with the last token of the text encoder; up to t = 950 of 1000.
trained_on: Pick-a-Pic v1 filtered to 168,539 win-lose pairs and 8,537 ties, Bradley-Terry loss on two noised images under one prompt, uniform t; U-Net and text encoder trainable.
score_enters: No gradient: the score ranks K = 4 sampled candidates per step, and the best and worst become a training pair for a LoRA fine-tune.
adding_scores: not addressed; the only feature arithmetic is a guidance-style boost on the middle-block feature (Eq. 8).
properties: Counting, attribute binding, spatial relation, position and prompt match are measured on images from the fine-tuned model through GenEval and T2I-CompBench++; object size is not tested.
unseen: no: evaluation uses 500 unique validation prompts and withholds no concept.
headline: T2I-CompBench++ 2D-Spatial (0 to 1, higher better) on SDXL rises from 0.1936 to 0.2414 after LPO fine-tuning, against 0.2406 for InterComp; GenEval Position rises from 9.25% to 14.00%.
copy_or_avoid: Copy the true timestep input and the focus on the first steps; avoid spatial pooling and two-images-one-sentence training for left-right and binding sentence pairs (inferred).

disagreements.claim: A noise-aware reward model is evidence that a score can steer sampling.
disagreements.paper_says: The score only selects sampled candidates for fine-tuning; reward fine-tuning with the LRM is listed as future work.

disagreements.claim: The reward model is reliable at high noise.
disagreements.source: the paper's framing on p. 2 and p. 9
disagreements.paper_says: Direct preference accuracy is reported only at t = 0 and t = 200 (Table 18); high-noise reliability is supported only by downstream metrics.
